summary: Session 3 (renumbered from 4 by operator decision): the extension now GUARANTEES the router its module launchers require, and refuses to half-finish when it cannot. Session 2 made every module command shell out to `python -m ai_router.modules`; nothing guaranteed that module was present or new enough, and the gap had a named victim -- a developer whose .venv held an older `dabbler-ai-router` would take the Marketplace update and then fail every module command, with re-running setup unable to help because a plain `pip install` reports an existing install as already-satisfied. Three things close it. (1) A version floor declared ONCE: `MINIMUM_ROUTER_VERSION` + the `PYPI_REQUIREMENT` derived from it, read by both the install path and the precondition (L-069-1), with `mode: install` now passing `--upgrade` so an older installation is upgraded rather than accepted. (2) A capability precondition that asks the interpreter the LAUNCHERS resolve to import `ai_router.modules`, never inferring success from pip's exit code (L-125-1), with no fail-open branch: a failed probe makes the install report failure. (3) A retryable scaffold: default-module creation is gated on the module being ABSENT rather than on whether that call created docs/modules.yaml, so a retry after a failed install recovers instead of being locked out behind a file nobody told the user about. Proven from a genuinely empty folder by a new `npm run test:dogfood` lane (real venv, real network pip, production handoff verbatim), wired into CI on Linux and Windows.

reason.specifics: FRESH EYES PREFERRED. Session 4 (the append-file partitioning, renumbered from 3) is INDEPENDENT of Sessions 1-3: it touches ai_router/ and docs/ rather than the extension's install and scaffold surfaces, and it carries no residual from this session. Nothing about it is continuation work, so there is no same-surface argument for continuity. Its risk is concentrated in one place the spec already names: the concatenated view must stay BYTE-IDENTICAL to what the unpartitioned file produced, with a round-trip falsifier -- a partitioning that quietly reorders history is worse than the conflict it removes. Whoever runs it should read this session's round-3 finding as a cautionary tale: the first fix for a real defect introduced a worse one, and only a falsifier pinning WHEN a value was resolved caught it.

residuals.source: Carried in from Session 2's disposition (where it names its owner as 'Session 4' under the pre-renumbering numbering)
residuals.description: Nothing in the automated suite asserts that the PUBLISHED `dabbler-ai-router` wheel is compatible with the shipping extension. The pre-release lanes install THIS checkout via the harness-only `DABBLER_ROUTER_INSTALL_SPEC` override, because a wheel cannot contain code that has not been published yet.
residuals.rationale: Partially discharged, deliberately not fully. This session made the check EXECUTABLE and gave it one source of truth: `MINIMUM_ROUTER_VERSION` is the floor, `probeRouterCapability` is the check, and both are exported. What remains is the half only the operator can run, because it depends on an act only the operator performs. The set's spec already mandates the ordering -- publish `dabbler-ai-router` first, CONFIRM THE WHEEL IS LIVE, then publish the extension -- and the post-publish step is now one command: create a throwaway venv, `pip install dabbler-ai-router` from the real registry, and run the probe body (`ROUTER_CAPABILITY_PROBE_CODE`) against it. If that import fails, the extension must not be published. Automating it pre-release is impossible; automating it post-publish would gate a release on a job that can only run after the release.
residuals.owner: operator (release walk, immediately after this set lands)
residuals.owner_rationale: Publishing is operator-only authority in every case, and this is the one assertion that can only be made once the wheel exists. It protects every existing project taking the Marketplace update.

residuals.source: Carried in from Session 2; re-observed this session
residuals.description: Layer 3 is worker-count sensitive on this hardware: at the local default of 4 workers specs intermittently fail waiting for the first tree row, while at 2 workers -- the count CI uses -- the suite is green.
residuals.rationale: Unchanged this session and not re-litigated. The run of record was taken at 2 workers and is recorded as such: 31/31 in 6.7 minutes with no failures, so this session adds a clean data point rather than new evidence of the flake. Still worth deciding whether the local default should simply match CI.
residuals.owner_rationale: Belongs with whoever next revisits Layer 3 runtime/parallelism; the Step 9 review should decide whether lowering the local default earns its own change.

residuals.description: The shared doc-walk in `ai_router/scripts/drift_guard.py` had no exclusion for setuptools build output, so `build/lib/` -- a verbatim copy of the package source that any `pip install` of this checkout materializes -- was scanned, and the anti-resurrection guard reported its OWN copied pattern table as live declarations. A green tree went red purely because someone had run an install.
residuals.rationale: Fixed here rather than deferred: this session's dogfood lane runs `pip install -e <repo>`, so it recreates the condition on every run, which makes the defect tightly coupled to the change rather than an unrelated pre-existing bug. `build` and `.eggs` join the existing `dist` / `out` / `test-results` entries -- the same class -- and a falsifier pins the exclusion narrow: a DIRECTORY named `build` is skipped, a FILE named `build.py` is still scanned, so the fix for a false positive cannot become a blanket that hides real violations.
residuals.owner_rationale: Closed here; classified A4.2 by `post_round_delta` and settled by a delta-scoped remediation-review (round 5, VERIFIED).
